correctness.rationale: Explicit projective reduction gives u(t)=u_0 exp(-2 gamma lambda t), and a direct Hessian/Householder product gives a scalar-plus-skew X equation. Exact logarithmic-norm integration proves the sech profile, unique peak and return time, global convergence and exceptional eigenline for every positive parameter; 192 original-system IVP integrations with four checkpoints each and symbolic identities were checked. Boundary cases u_0=0, |u_0|=1, v_1=0 and X_0=0 are explicitly covered. Computations corroborate rather than prove the infinite assertion. Uniform projective orientation has acute-angle density 2/pi; integrating the exact deterministic peak law yields P(G>z)=arcsin(z^(-2 gamma/beta))/pi for z>=1 and the moment finiteness criterion p<2 gamma/beta. Numerical midpoint angular quadrature of 200000 directions supports the formula.

originality.rationale: The coupled equations and the Oja direction solution are prior art, but their statements do not imply the new quantitative coupled-position claim. Full primary comparisons and targeted mathematical-record searches revealed no prior sharp hyperbolic-secant norm profile, exact unbounded gain exponent and global convergent-but-transient classification for the balanced quadratic saddle. This is best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness certificate. The random-orientation peak-risk tail likewise is not a statement or implication of the available local stability or Oja direction-only theorems. Distinct heavy-tail laws for randomized heavy-ball parameters and Sylvester trial spaces are not equivalent.
residual_risks: Unindexed or uninspected older dynamical-systems and computational-chemistry literature could contain an equivalent two-mode coupled-flow calculation.
Equal absolute Hessian eigenvalues are nongeneric; no claim extends to anisotropic nonlinear saddles.
Same-model originality review is not an independent historical-priority audit.

value.rationale: The direction alignment error is a natural control variable in the original coupled saddle-search flow. The sharp formula demonstrates arbitrarily large transient position deviations even throughout a full-measure globally convergent direction basin, and supplies a universal sech pulse, exact peak/recovery clock and divergence exponent. These quantify a meaningful mechanism not available from the known local asymptotic convergence statement; no general nonlinear theorem is claimed. For Haar-uniform initial search lines, the deterministic transient becomes a power-tailed random variable and even its mean diverges when beta>=2 gamma, despite almost-sure convergence; this explicitly quantifies the risk of unconstrained direction initialization.
